newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour declines comment on monetary mtg rumours.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour declines comment on monetary mtg rumours.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party declined comment on rumours among some bond market operators that a monetary meeting scheduled for May 7 would be postponed if it won Thursday's election.
"We never comment on rumours," a spokesman for Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown told Reuters.
The next monetary meeting between Bank of England Governor Eddie George and the Chancellor of the Exchequer -- whoever that will be -- has been provisionally scheduled for May 7.
Bond market operators said there had been rumours that, if elected, Brown might postpone the meeting to allow time to set up his new monetary policy framework.
Labour plans to establish a new monetary policy committee at the Bank of England and a council of economic advisers at the Treasury.

Minutes of the last monetary meeting between George and Conservative Chancellor Kenneth Clarke on April 10 will be published on May 21. Interest rates were left unchanged at 6.0 percent after that meeting.
